utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber has been informed that there are matters which the Prosecution wishes to raise. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. It's just a question of scheduling of witnesses. The next witness is Blaz Paradzik, as you know. He's waiting to proceed and is waiting outside. I'm also hopeful that his evidence will be brief, at least fairly short compared to many of the other witnesses in the case. And there may arise a situation tomorrow whereby we finish early. I have made arrangements to bring in another witness whom my colleague Mr. Weiner is hopefully going to start proofing this afternoon. That's Mr. Ibro Taletovic. And if, as I think we will, finish well before tomorrow, we can start that witness at some point tomorrow afternoon. The situation, however, will arise that the next witness after him, Alija Fitozovic, who is I think a reasonably important witness, will be flying in on Friday, the day that the Trial Chamber is not sitting. His proofing can proceed over the weekend. That's not a problem. He will be ready to go Monday morning. He has to fly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Monday afternoon. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. Monday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because we're still in May next week. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Sorry. Monday afternoon. Now, I'm handling that particular witness, and I've got several reasons for asking that we be -- the Prosecution be granted permission to interpose him in the evidence of Taletovic on Monday if that situation arises. First of all, Mr. Taletovic is, because of his residence, the place that he lives, is a witness who is a lot easier to get here to the Tribunal than Alija Fitozovic, who has to be flown in from the former Yugoslavia. So keeping Alija Fitozovic here is going to be more expensive, a greater strain on him, and for those considerations, I suggest it makes good practical sense to deal with him as quickly as we can. Secondly, if we deal with him as quickly as we can next week that frees me up to go and deal with Todorovic and have him come in smoothly after Fitozovic and that's what I am hoping will happen. Now, Mr. Taletovic could come back at some later stage. If that arrangement is suitable, can we proceed on that basis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the Trial Chamber will have no problems with that, because what is important is to get on with the evidence, the viva voce evidence witnesses as much as possible. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If I'm wrong in my estimation that this next witness will finish quickly and we go with him all of tomorrow as well, then the exercise with Mr. Taletovic will not have been wasted because valuable proofing exercise will have been completed in any event and we'll be ready to slot him in smoothly at some point in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the Defence have to prepare for something like three witnesses, apart from the one coming now. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. They've received the proofing notes from that witness. But they have to be prepared for tomorrow afternoon -- if we finish this witness tomorrow afternoon early, they have to be prepared for Mr. Taletovic to come in to fill in the rest of the time. And then they have to be prepared, if you accept my proposal, on Monday afternoon to kick off -- to start with Alija Fitozovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Alija Fitozovic, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: So can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think that is clear, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Is that suitable to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, that would be okay to the Chamber, as long as we don't waste any time waiting for our witness. It's practical to get somebody else in the meantime. MR. DI FAZIO: That's what I'm trying to avoid and that's why I've asked for that arrangement. Thank you, if Your Honours please, and may the next witness be called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. The Prosecution, you can start. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: In Prud, municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to remind the Chamber, is Prud a small town or village just across the Bosna River from the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. It's a smaller place. It's a village on the left bank of the River Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is its population predominantly of one ethnic group or another?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. It's mostly of one ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what ethnic group is that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If asked to describe your ethnic background, what would you say it is?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I am a Croat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Where were you educated?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: In Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What level of education did you achieve?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: A secondary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the former Yugoslavia, it was common for men to perform military service. Did you perform military service, and if so, what years did you perform it in?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. I performed it in 1972.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Chamber of your working career, and in particular, I'm interested to know the sort of work that you were doing in the months prior to April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I was employed at the company called Hidroput from Sisak in Croatia. I resided in Prud when it wasn't working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what sort of work did you do with the company Hidroput?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I was a manager.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what does Hidroput do? What sort of work does it perform?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It is a company that deals with shipping on water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does it deal with shipping and boating that took place on the rivers of the former Yugoslavia, including the Sava and so on?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever been a member of the Communist Party of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever join any political party in the -- whilst living in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what political party was that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. I was a member of the Croatian Democratic Union, the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you join the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not in dispute in this case that hostilities broke out in Bosanski Samac on the night of the 16th and 17th of April, 1992. Thinking back, how long before that had you joined the HDZ? Was it in the same year?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure exactly about the date. I might have joined a little bit earlier than that, but I don't recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's okay. I'm not asking for a precise date. Is it the case that you were a member of the HDZ for only a matter of months before the events in April of 1992 in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In that year of 1992, were you a member of any form or type of local commune that existed in Prud?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. I was the vice-president of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly explain to the Chamber what the local commune was, how it was formed, and what sort of tasks it undertook?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: After the multiparty elections in Bosnia-Herzegovina, a local commune was formed from the winner party. In my town, the HDZ won. And members of the party became members of the local commune. The positions were unsalaried. We weren't professionals. And we took care of the needs that existed in the town of Prud. We took care of everybody, of everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you were charged with the responsibility of dealing with local issues affecting the town, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: More or less we were charged with the responsibilities in our town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And had this system of local communes been in existence in the former Yugoslavia for some time prior to the multiparty elections? In other words, was it a common feature of life in small towns in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. It existed in the former Yugoslavia as well. This same organisation continued. It was some form of local self-management. It was quite normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll return to the local communes at a later point. I want to ask you if you know a gentleman named Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him, and can you comment on the type of relationship that you had with him, namely, whether you were friends, acquaintances, or you just knew who the person was.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I knew him. We weren't friends, but we weren't acquaintances. Well, I knew him, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he once treat your mother in relation to her dialysis treatment for kidney problems?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look around the room and see if you can see him. If you can, point him out, please.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: The gentleman with the beard, in the middle. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Can the record indicate that the witness identified Mr. Simic, Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a gentleman named Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname Brko?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long would you say that you've known him?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: About 30 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, can you carry out the same exercise. Look around the room and see if you can identify him; if you can, point him out.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: He's the first from that side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does he have any facial hair?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: He has a moustache. He's grey-haired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the record indicate that the witness has correctly identified Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other gentleman I want to ask you about is Simo Zaric. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Same thing: About 30 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the past, have you had conversations with him?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've heard him speak, heard his voice?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever play soccer with him?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. That was our hobby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in a football club called the Veteran, or Veteran Football Club?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it was called. The people that were playing football recreationally and were a little bit older were called the Veterans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was on the team with you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had numerous occasions, I take it, to speak with him and hear him speak, hear his voice?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that you've known him about 30 years. Can you recall approximately when you first met him?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: While he was in secondary school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you at secondary school as well?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: That's since we've known each other. That's when we started talking to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever drunk with him or attended social occasions with him?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you conduct the same exercise that you did in respect of the other two and have a look around and see if you can identify him.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: The gentleman with the red tie. MR. DI FAZIO: I can't see the tie that Mr. Simic [sic] is wearing. I'm hoping it's red. If it is, can the record indicate that the witness has correctly identified Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Page 9, line 23. I didn't hear, actually, the original, what Mr. Di Fazio said. It's not Mr. Simic. I suppose it should be Mr. Zaric, with regard to the tie. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can correct that. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Pantelic is quite correct. I don't think there's any dispute that the witness identified Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the period of time leading up to April of 1992, was there a degree of tension building up in the area that you lived in at that time, around Prud, Bosanski Samac, and so on?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were civilians arming themselves?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you possess any weapons yourself?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of weapons did you possess?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Hunting weapons. Carbine and a hunting rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those weapons licensed, fully licensed?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've already described that tension was rising in the former Yugoslavia. Was there the appearance, the emerging appearance, of checkpoints at various towns and villages in the municipality of Bosanski Samac and indeed in the general area around your town?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the positioning of checkpoints a matter that local town communes were interested in and would meet to discuss?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. They were interested in that, and it was discussed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around your village or town of Prud, were there other villages which were inhabited mainly by people of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there just such a village named Struke, S-t-r-u-k-e?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how far is that from Prud?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It's in the same line as Prud and almost forms one whole with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So in terms of actual buildings and structure, it looks as if it's part of the same town as Prud?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: You could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, Serbs live in Struke and Croats live mainly in Prud?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the months, the two or three months leading up to -- perhaps I'll rephrase that. In the early part of 1992, did the residents of Struke indicate any desire in regard of the setting up of checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the positioning of checkpoints in Struke a matter that local communes became involved in?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were meetings held? And I should add: Were meetings held to discuss that issue, the positioning of checkpoints in Struke?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend such meetings?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber why the residents of Struke wanted to establish checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It was customary for us to hold meetings. Parts of local communes of the Odzak municipality and certain warnings were issued, or announcements were made, that they wished to install checkpoints at the entrance to Prud. We were taken aback by such a proposition, and we couldn't understand why they would want to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you to pause there, and perhaps we can add a bit more detail to your account as we go along. You say "They wished to install checkpoints." Who precisely wanted to install checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: The inhabitants of Struke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you say that, "We were taken aback by such a proposition." Who is the "we" that you refer to?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I mean the local commune of Prud.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. That's clarified things. Now, please continue in your account.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Then we convened a meeting. In fact, we scheduled a meeting to be held in Struke to clear up this matter and see why it is necessary to have a checkpoint in Prud. At that meeting, the representatives of the population of Struke stated that they had reason to fear that somebody from Croatia might come and carry out a sabotage action. As for us from the local commune, they said they were not afraid of us and they didn't think that we could do something like that, whereas we, on our part, gave them assurances that no danger is emanating from us and we will never do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, can you tell us the approximate date or time of this particular meeting that you've just been describing.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: That meeting was held on the 29th, around noon, I believe, 11.00 or 12.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 29th of what month, what year?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: 29th February 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And where was the meeting held?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: In Struke, in a privately owned house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the people who were attending the meeting, were they members of the local commune of Struke and Prud?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Members of the local commune of Prud attended, whereas Struke did not have a local commune. They were part of the local commune of Dubica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Were the opposite parties, so to speak, members of the local commune of Dubica who were attending?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it your understanding that the meeting was to be attended by primarily representatives of local communes?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Local people discussing a local issue: Was that to be the make-up of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way it was conceived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I wonder whether the witness would be able to tell us where the checkpoints were located. Were they around the perimeter of Struke and Prud taken together, or was there some type of demarcation line with checkpoints between Struke and Prud proper? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the inquiry by the Chamber is basically as to the location of the proposed checkpoints. Can you tell us or give us any idea of where it was proposed that these checkpoints would be placed?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Until then, there were no checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. But was there any proposal that they be placed at specific locations, locations that you were aware of or that representatives of the Prud local commune were aware of, or is it the case that they were simply discussing the establishment of checkpoints without details as to where they might be put up?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. There was talk about putting up one checkpoint, one single, in Struke.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: And I don't know the exact location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at the meeting, did any other uninvited guests appear?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This question should be rephrased. It's calling for speculation how this witness can know whether the guest is invited or uninvited. So it's a matter -- uninvited. MR. DI FAZIO: It's also on oxymoron. I don't suppose a guest can be uninvited.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody appear at the meeting whom you did not expect to see?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: At some point towards the end of the meeting, Mr. Simic appeared, along with Mr. Tadic, Mr. Rajko Djuric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just ask you this: Mr. Simic, what is the first name of the Mr. Simic that you refer to?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Dr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Tadic that you've referred to, is that Mr. Miroslav Tadic whom you identified earlier?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the other man that you mentioned, Rajko Djuric, did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. His nickname was Truman, and he was from Donja Dubica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the political affiliations of those three people?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Rajko Djuric was a member of the SDS. Dr. Blagoje Simic was a member of the SDS. And I'm not sure about Miroslav Tadic, which party he belonged to at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You qualify that. You don't know which party he was a member of at that time. Did you ever know him to be a member of any party at any time? If you don't know, say so.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: He used to be a member of the SKJ, which is the League of Communists of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, you said that these were unexpected arrivals. Can you tell the Chamber if any of them addressed the meeting of these two communes?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Simic addressed those of us present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What announcements or utterances were made?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Dr. Simic took the floor, greeted us, and said that he had just left another meeting or session where the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac was proclaimed, and that municipality encompassed all the villages of Bosanski Samac municipality with a Serb population, as well as the villages of Odzak municipality, namely, Donja Dubica, Novi Grad, Struke, and Trnjak. Only Struke and Trnjak were part of Donja Dubica at the time. In fact, the villages from the Odzak municipality were joining this new entity, this new Serb municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, had you gone to the meeting intending to discuss anything other than the establishment of checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No. We did not intend to discuss anything else. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Can the witness be shown P11, please. Perhaps for the sake of ease of understanding the evidence the English version could be put on the ELMO and the witness could read from the B/C/S, unless the Chamber -- members of the Tribunal -- sorry, the Chamber have their own copies. I don't know if you do. Then perhaps it could be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we can have it on the ELMO, please. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, witness, that document speaks for itself. It proclaims itself to be a decision on the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac and the Serbian municipality of Pelagicevo in the process of being established. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, can you recall if Mr. Blagoje Simic made reference to Serbian municipalities of Pelagicevo, or is it that your memory only tells you he spoke about the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No, I don't recall anything about Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Cast your eye over Article 2 and the names of the settlements that are listed there. And once you have done that, can you tell us if they were settlements mentioned by Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, he did mention that. He mentioned Novi Grad and Donja Dubica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the others that are listed there? Did he mention those?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No, he didn't mention them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you turn to the second page of the document. It is dated the 29th of February, 1992 and apparently signed by one Ilija Ristic. Do you know Ilija Ristic?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: He was a veterinarian doctor. He worked at the veterinarian station of Bosanski Samac, veterinarian clinic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm done with that document. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone speak to him about the rearrangements of municipalities, challenge him on it? By that I mean the assembled local commune delegates.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they say?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I specifically addressed Rajko Djuric, not Simic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I asked how they intended to link up with Samac municipality, since between Donja Dubica and Samac my home village, Prud, is located. I asked him how they intended to establish the link with Samac municipality, and he answered that they were planning to do it via Struke and the Bosna River. They were either going to build a bridge or organise a ferry service or something like that. And it was precisely there that they wanted to put up a checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition to the rearranging of municipalities for Bosanski Samac and Odzak, was there any talk of the municipality of Bosanski Brod?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Not at that meeting. There were other meetings where it was discussed. Yes. Serb villages from Odzak municipality were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's be clear so that we understand what you're saying, okay? First of all, I'll go back to my original question, and that's this: At the meeting - this is on the 29th of February, the one that Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Truman attended - was there any talk by any one of those three men regarding possible rearrangements of municipal lines vis-a-vis Bosanski Brod?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: On that occasion it was mentioned that villages bordering on Bosanski Brod, Serb villages, that is, will be joining Bosanski Brod municipality, while villages bordering on Modrica would be joining Modrica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which of the three men made that announcement?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Rajko Djuric made the announcement, and Dr. Simic did not deny any of it. He also confirmed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that last part of your answer, I take it Dr. Blagoje Simic confirmed what Djuric, or Truman, had said regarding Bosanski Brod.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he actually discuss that particular matter, by that I mean Blagoje Simic, did he actually talk about what would be happening to Bosanski Brod?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were his comments, therefore, limited to confirming what Truman had said?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any reference or talk made to the JNA, the Yugoslav army, at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. There was always talk about that between the local communes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What I'm particularly interested in is this: Did any of the three men who arrived - Dr. Blagoje Simic, Truman, or Miroslav Tadic - refer or talk about the JNA at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was said?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Dr. Simic said that the JNA would enter the Serb villages, whether the others liked it or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall how he -- how it was that he came to be making this statement, how the utterance came about, how it arose in the context of what was happening at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: He said during his address, when he mentioned the proclamation of the Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac, he said that the JNA would protect the Serb population and enter Serb villages, and this was because the municipality of Odzak resisted the JNA presence in these areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he talking about, as far as you were aware, when he referred to the municipality of Odzak resisting JNA pressure?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: At that meeting he just held a speech and he didn't say anything else. The meeting lost all its meaning after the speech, and it was completed. It was finished after we found out that the Serb municipality of Bosanski Samac had been proclaimed. That was the first time we heard of that event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly do you mean when you say "The meeting lost its meaning after the speech"? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: We were taken aback. These settlements didn't belong to the municipality of Odzak any more. That was new information for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there much talking going on after this announcement had been made?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you describe the tone of the meeting following the completion of these announcements?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Dr. Simic held his speech. They stayed a little bit longer and then they left. So they just gave this announcement to us and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the three of them leave together?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have a chance to discuss the issue of the setting up of checkpoints again?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It wasn't really demanded, not with regard to setting up checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Up until that time, you had not heard of these new plans for redistribution of municipal lines. Following that visit, can you tell us if these plans became well known amongst the population in Prud and in the surrounding villages and towns?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think the words "plans" which were used by my learned friend, according to the fact that this witness just said, I'm speaking about the event in this village Struke, is not appropriate. In fact, maybe we could speak about the decision or the fact that it was an announcement. But the plans are a little bit -- could be dubious and could be two-folded or it's not so certain. I mean, it's not in dispute that this decision which is actually the Exhibit P11 was made. So let's be more precise. Because otherwise the Prosecution might through these questions create a theory which is absolutely wrong of course from the side of the Defence that there were certain plans of dividing this area. So if we are speaking strictly about the exhibits, if we are speaking about the documents, then we should use more precise words. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: It's difficult to think of anything that would require more planning than a decision to carve up municipalities, if Your Honours please, almost beyond comprehension. It matters not, I submit, if Mr. Pantelic is happy with announcement, pronouncement, proclamation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Announcement of the decision. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Announcement of the decision is fine by me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any -- I withdraw that. Can you tell us if the announcements of Dr. Blagoje Simic, or ones that he conveyed to you at that meeting, became common knowledge in Prud and the surrounding towns and villages?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, you heard the objection of Defence counsel that there is no -- the word "plan" was inaccurate. Did you hear anyone referring to -- in the community, I mean - referring to the announcements as plans for the future, plans to recarve, redesignate municipal lines?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Not before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not before what?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Before that day when I heard about the formation of the Serbian municipality of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What about after that day? Was there discussion in the community, the town of Prud and surroundings towns in Bosanski Samac and the municipality of Bosanski Samac of intentions to carve up or redesignate municipal lines?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to people about these plans?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I didn't speak to anybody, but I heard it from others that they did talk amongst themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before the events of the 16th and 17th of April 1992, but after this meeting that you've just bee describing at Struke, did you ever hear of Mr. Blagoje Simic addressing or attending any other meetings where this sort of topic was discussed?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify the meeting that you heard that he attended? By identify, I mean can you give us an idea of about when this meeting was, or where it was held?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I think this meeting was held after the one that I was at. I can't remember the time. It might have been March of 1992. I think this was an inter-party meeting between representatives of SDS, HDZ. I'm not sure if the representatives of the SDA were present as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just to be clear, you are reporting now -- making reports of a meeting that you personally did not attend; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the evidence that you're about to give is based on matters that you have been told; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that case, I'd like you to identify your sources of information. First of all, did any individuals report to you or tell you or describe to you this meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. There were more persons that told me what was being discussed at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us the names of these people who told you and described to you the meeting, and also their positions, I mean political positions, if they held any.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: At this meeting, the following people were present: Mato Nujic, president of the municipality of Bosanski Samac; Mato Madzarevic. He worked at the municipality. He was responsible for one section, for one department. Filip Evic, the president of the HDZ; Blazanovic. I can't remember his first name. He's from Grebnice. Slavko Matic, secretary of the HDZ. I don't know if anyone else was present, but I remember these men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And they're all, I take it, Croats and all members of the HDZ?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they all describe to you and tell you what happened at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they all essentially provide you with the same account of events at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody was there when they were recounting this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question. My question is this: Did they all provide you with the same account of how things had transpired, taken place, at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from reports from these particular individuals who were present at the meeting, was there a degree of common knowledge in the community as to the fact of the meeting and what it taken place at the meeting? In other words, was it widely known throughout your community and the surrounding towns and villages?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the discussion became widely known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what did you hear took place at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I heard from these gentlemen present here that Mr. Blagoje Simic had told them that Prud was joining Odzak --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I heard from those gentleman not present here. Part of Bazik, Domaljevac, were going to join Orasje, whereas other settlements would remain within Bosanski Samac. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any discussion as to what might happen to Croatian villages in these newly designated municipalities?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. They asked Mr. Simic what was going to happen to the other Croatian settlements that were to remain in the municipality of Samac, what he intended to do with them. And then he said that they would guarantee them security to -- they would guarantee security to whoever wanted to remain, and those people that did not want to remain there could exchange their property and everything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And was that last remark apparently attributed to Mr. Blagoje Simic?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I wonder whether you could seek a clarification from the witness, page 26, line 3, re: "Those that did not want to remain there could exchange their property and everything else." Could you find out what the witness exactly means by that? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I appreciate that you're telling the Chamber reports of what other people told you and you weren't at the meeting, but the inquiry of the Chamber is that can you provide any clarification as to what you mean by having said that Mr. Blagoje Simic apparently said that people could remain in the new municipalities or could exchange their property and everything else? Have you got -- was there any explanation given to you as to what that meant: "exchanging their property and everything else"?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It wasn't explained, but at that time rumours were already abounding about the corridor, and so these areas had to remain in the same municipality. But whoever didn't like that had to leave. Whoever disagreed with that kind of a solution could choose to stay, to swap their property, or to sell it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've mention that had a number of HDZ men reported to you what had happened at the meeting and what Blagoje Simic had said at the meeting, and so on. Did those HDZ personalities that you mentioned explain to you what Blagoje Simic had meant by saying that people could remain in the new municipalities or exchange their property and everything else? If they didn't tell you what he meant, that's fine, but we just want to know, if he did provide you with an explanation, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: They didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have in your own mind an idea of what it meant?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: In my personal opinion, this meant that there could be clashes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you be a little more precise? What exactly do you mean by that, and why did you think that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I knew that these Croatian villages did not want to stay in that kind of a municipality of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it that that you thought might lead to conflict?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Well, I didn't think about those issues at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm fearful that if I plumb this topic any further we'll be moving into real speculation. It would be better if I left it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It depends on what type of evidence you want to elicit from the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Paradzik, I want to move on now to a completely different topic, and that is the events of the night of the 16th and 17th of April, 1992. On that night, were you at home in Prud?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the night did you hear the sound of gunfire and firearms?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you wake up and go out and investigate the situation?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did men gather in the centre of Prud?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: About 200.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were some of them armed; and if so, with what?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: They had -- those of them that were armed brought their own personal weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of weapons were they in the main? Hunting rifles, Kalashnikovs, AK-47s? What sort of weaponry are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Hunting rifles and other types of rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a community leader, you're in the local commune. Can you tell us if there were any plans that had been laid as to what to do in precisely just such a situation, organisational plans of how to respond to this sort of crisis?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the plan?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: To evacuate women and children to Croatia, the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Evacuate women and children from where?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: From Prud. At that time it was already night. So from Prud and from Samac, if anybody came from Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So the plans that were afoot or already laid included evacuation of women and children from Bosanski Samac as well, if they came?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the only way to come from Bosanski Samac to Prud across a small bridge across the River Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Would that be an appropriate moment, if Your Honours please, to break for the afternoon break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break until 1615 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Prosecution continues. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were telling us about the events on the night of the 16th and 17th of April and the plans that had been laid in the event of trouble and that they included evacuation. Did the plans include or call for any sort of armed intervention on the part of the men who were gathered there?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: In the event of an attack on the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you plan to defend yourselves?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know a gentleman named Namik Suljic?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was he, and was he gathered with the other men there, in Prud, I mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: He was on the reserve force of the police, and his position was that of deputy commander of the police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During the course of the evening, did any -- I mean by that during the night, when it was still dark - did anyone try to cross over from Bosanski Samac to Prud?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people try and cross over during the day?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there more people crossing or attempting to cross the bridge during the day than at night?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Mainly during the day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there any fire directed towards the bridge during the night, weapons fire, I mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Occasionally. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown the photographs -- I think they're P14 or P14A. In any event, my intention is to show the unlabelled photographs, whichever exhibit it is. Perhaps the Court can assist me by telling me which is the unlabelled version.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is P14A, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Can that be produced to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Which photograph exactly? I'm sorry. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry. F34 and F35. And perhaps, Mr. Usher, F34 could be shown first on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, just have a look at that photograph and tell us what it depicts.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It's the destroyed bridge between Prud and Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As we look at the photograph, are we looking from the direction of Bosanski Samac and towards Prud?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Looking from the direction of Bosanski Samac towards Prud.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the river that we can see is the Bosna?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the background of the photograph you see a line of trees, and you can't really see any buildings. Is Prud to be found just past the line of trees, and is it obscured by the trees in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, it is obscured by the trees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question. What sort of bridge was it in April 1992? You can't really tell from looking at that photograph what sort of bridge it was.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It was a one-way bridge, a bridge for one-way traffic, with traffic lights. It was not two-way. I think its carrying capacity was two and a half tonnes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So you could get across it in a car, could you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, you could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I've finished with that photograph. And, Mr. Usher, on reflection, I don't need to use the other photograph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I was asking you about any weapons fire directed towards the bridge. Was there any directed towards the bridge during the day, that is, during the day of the 17th?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of weaponry was trained against the bridge on that day, during the day?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Fire was opened from machine-guns, snipers, and tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the bridge eventually destroyed by tank fire?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It was damaged, not completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the fire coming from, the fire directed towards the bridge?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: We assumed that the tank was located on the separation line at the entrance to Samac, and that's from where fire was opened. Several kilometres away from the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. What I'm interested in is this: You've --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Just a matter of clarification of transcript, because here it said "separation line." Actually, what I know about Bosanski Samac is that it is a company named Separacija. There were no particular - on 17 or something - like separation line. So it's actually a company called Separacija, separation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Mr. Di Fazio can you clarify that? MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned that this tank that was directing its fire towards the bridge was located on a line. What sort of line was it? How would you describe that line where the tank was?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: The tank was in the compound of Separacija. That was the only place from which you could hit the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Separacija a company or an institution?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes. It was an enterprise dealing with gravel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm not actually terribly interested in where the weapons were based. What I'm interested in most of all is this: Was the weapons fire, machine-gun, tank fire, whatever sort of fire that was directed towards the bridge coming from the Bosanski Samac side or from the Prud side? That's what I want to know.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: From the side of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the damage to the bridge during the day of the 17th of April 1992 bring a halt to the flow of people across the bridge?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: After the bridge was hit, nobody attempted to cross it any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have described it as a flow of people across a bridge, but that may not be correct. Can you tell us what the true situation is? Were there a lot of people crossing? Were people coming across in dribs and drabs? Was it a constant flow? And do you have any idea of numbers of people who got across the bridge?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I don't have a number for you. Anybody who was able to reach the bridge would cross it. People crossed over in groups, and this continued until 2.00 on the 17th, after which time it was no longer possible because the bridge was constantly under fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic background of people who were crossing the bridge?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: They were mostly Muslims, Bosniaks, and a smaller number of Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see anything on the bridge that could attract fire, for example, gun emplacements, soldiers' nests, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now cast your mind back to the events of the night, during the night, and after you had woken up and gone into the centre of the town. Did anyone there in Prud have a radio?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who had a radio?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Namik Suljic. After the police withdrew from the bridge, he came to Prud and left a radio, or rather, a Motorola, on the premises of the community centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, before we get into the radio, you say that police withdrew from the bridge. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I mean the reserve police. They had been on the bridge between Samac and Prud and they had come from the territory of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of numbers of reserve police are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It was one shift's worth of people, whether it was two, three, or four, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But that sort of order of numbers: Two or three or four?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. And Namik Suljic, was he one of these policemen who was guarding the bridge, or who had been guarding the bridge?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: He wasn't guarding the bridge. He was a commander and he crossed the bridge as a commander, in that capacity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The policemen who had been on the bridge, was it their function to guard the bridge?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I don't know. They were not able to -- they were not capable of guarding it. I don't know what they were doing. At any rate, there were threats that the bridge could be blown up, that mines could be laid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the preceding weeks and months, had it been customary to keep policemen posted on that bridge at night?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I don't know when permanent duty service was introduced, but at a certain point, standing guard duty was introduced on the bridge between Prud and Samac and between Slavonski and Bosanski Samac, on the Sava River. But I wouldn't be able to tell you the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said that Namik Suljic left a Motorola radio on the premises at the community centre. Were you also there at the community centre?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there other men gathered there?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Motorola radio functioning? Was it operational? Was it picking up signals, receiving signals?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was someone changing frequency on the radio?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear the sound of the voice of any of the defendants on the radio that night?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose voice did you hear?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I heard the voice of Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was he saying?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: He was communicating through the radio, calling seagull, seagull 1, 2, and 3. I don't know how many seagulls there were. And he identified himself as The Sea. He was some sort of centre to whom they were responding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So he used code, in effect, referring to himself as "The Sea" and others as a seagull followed by a number?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you can recall, was it apparent conversation in this sense: You could hear someone conversing with The Sea, or Mr. Zaric, and he was replying to that person, in other words, a two-way conversation overheard on radio?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear Mr. Zaric say?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: For instance, he would say, "Seagull 1, respond," and when they responded, he would say, "Shift forward," or "forward with your left wing." He would say things like, "Everything under control. How are things coming along?" things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all of it make sense to you?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I understood only one thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: When one of the Seagulls responded and said that he could hear columns of tanks moving in Prud, that was the only thing I could make out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how did you greet that assertion over the radio that there were tanks moving through Prud, you being in Prud, after all?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: We thought of it as a lie, because we knew there were no tanks and we knew who he was trying to scare off and intimidate with that sort of claim. And we just laughed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- I withdraw that. Is there any doubt in your mind that the voice that you heard was that of Simo Zaric?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No, no doubt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was April of 1992. You've said that you've known him for about 30 years. As at April of 1992, how long had you known him? Just think back and do some mental calculations. Use your high school years, if necessary, and tell us about how long you had known him in April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Would you care to clarify that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old were you in 1992? It's about 10 years ago, or it is 10 years ago.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I was 40.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you known Simo Zaric at that time? Did you meet him when you were a child, when you were a kid? Did you meet him in your teenage years? Did you meet him as a young man? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: In 1992 I had known him for about -- for more than 20 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've described various other forms of weaponry that were being used to attack the bridge during the day, tank and machine-gun fire. Did you ever see who was firing at the bridge?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Prud is now part of the Federation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following the events in April of 1992, did you remain in Prud or did you go elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: After the fall of Prud in the month of July, I left for Croatia [Realtime transcript read in error "left Croatia"].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that departure for Croatia, did you have an opportunity to speak to the people who were coming across the bridge and other people who might have escaped from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of those people ever complain to you of having to wear white armbands?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Those people that ran away, they didn't have to wear white armbands. Those that were exchanged told us what they had gone through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, we have to correct an answer by the witness, line 12. After the fall of Prud in the month of July, I left Croatia. Did he say he left for Croatia? MR. DI FAZIO: I believe that was -- that's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we clarify with the witness? MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In July, did you leave Prud and go to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the people who were exchanged complained to you of what they had gone through. Did they ever complain to you or describe to you having to wear white armbands?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I'm not sure. They had some kind of a mark that they had to wear. I don't know if these were white or not. They also had to do forced labour, dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they complain to you of this? That's what I want to know.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: In these conversations, they said that they had been beaten. Some men that were exchanged came with broken ribs. Their teeth had been pulled out. And we believed what they told us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of condition were the people who were exchanged -- what sort of condition were they in, physical condition, I mean?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: They were not all in the same physical condition. Some were in good physical condition but some also came in a very bad condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the war, were you ever arrested and tortured yourself?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to have only a few questions, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Paradzik. I am attorney at law Novak Lukic. I will ask you several questions on behalf of Miroslav Tadic's Defence. You described today this meeting on the 29th of February, 1992, and you mentioned that Miroslav Tadic also came to this meeting. I am interested in the following: Did Tadic say anything at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: He did not say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he participate in the discussions at all?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: No. He did not say a word. Tadic drove them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them being driven there by him? You gave a statement to the Prosecution in 1995. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You read -- you were read this statement and you signed it; is that correct? Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. The question on page 40, line 11, was not answered by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Actually, the witness nodded by his head, and so my colleague probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He did ask whether he saw him being driven. So if counsel can ask the question again so that we get the answer recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see Tadic driving Mr. Simic and the other gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I asked you the following. I asked you about the statement that you made in 1995. You said that you remember signing it.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take another look at this statement again before you came to testify here? If you did not, do you remember the details that you mentioned at that time to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I remember the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this statement, when you described this event that took place on the 29th of February of 1992, you said -- you only mentioned the name of Blagoje Simic to the OTP. You did not mention the name of Miroslav Tadic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I did mention it. It might be the case that it didn't go into the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how long they were at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Up to an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other counsel? Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I start with my cross-examination, let me -- thank you. Let me try to clarify one matter with regard to the translation of word "speculation," because I noticed even from the side of the witnesses appearing prior before this Trial Chamber, and also from my colleague's side and the defendant's side, that the translation of this word, "speculation" in B/C/S language is not proper. Usually the Translation Unit use the word "spekulacija," which in our meaning, in B/C/S language means that someone wants to speculate with money, with, you know, undercover, dishonestly and stuff like that. My suggestion would be that the word "speculation" from now on should be translated in, I will say in our language "predvidjanje pretpostavka," like the meaning of some kind of prediction or something like that in narrow sense. Because exact translation word, English word "speculation" into the B/C/S word "spekulacija" is absolutely confusing, even for witnesses, they made certain reactions prior in I think November/December last year. Then for my colleagues and for defendants too. Maybe we could hear something from the Translation Unit. MR. DI FAZIO: May I say something about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to allow the translation to be completed. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I've got a problem with that. First of all, I don't speak B/C/S, and as far as I'm aware, the Chamber doesn't speak B/C/S, and I don't think that Mr. Pantelic can restrict the interpretation of language in any particular way. The word "speculation" of course means speculation in the sense of wondering about something and also gambling and it has much the same meaning in English as well. All words have different meanings. They're rich in meaning. The proper job for interpretation is in the interpreter's booth. That's the place for the job to be done and they will do the best that they can. If language and meaning is not coming across accurately, in the view of Mr. Pantelic, then he is in the best position to take care of that. He is in the best position to simply ask the witness a question and clarify anything that he wants to, and he's got the weapon of cross-examination to do that if he wants to. So I suggest that we just go ahead in the way that we've been going on thus far and leave interpretation to the professionals, and anything that -- any further added meaning that Mr. Pantelic wants to add to what a witness has said, he's free to do so by the use of question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber doesn't think that there is any need to vary our procedures. We have competent interpreters, and if there is any problem, the correct procedures will be followed. And also, clarification can always be sought from the witness, so that the evidence given by the witness is correctly translated and is also properly understood by either counsel or the witness, or the defendants, whoever is having a problem. So can you just go ahead with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was just my suggestion with regard to the benefit of this trial proceeding, nothing more. I didn't give any orders or stuff like that. Well, I can proceed, of course. Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Paradzik, good afternoon. My name is Pantelic. I am the Defence counsel of Mr. Blagoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's try to clear up certain things before we start. I think this might have been a misunderstanding. We might have not been focused enough. When asked by my colleague of the Prosecution, you said that you became a member of the HDZ a few months before April 1992. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This topic is not very relevant, but we should clear up these issues because of the transcript. In the notes given to us by the Prosecution that are based on their interview with you, you said that you became a member of HDZ in 1990, before the elections, very soon after the party was founded. Do you remember saying this?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a suggestion. Why don't you finish -- why don't you wait until I finish with the question, make a pause, and then answer my question. So what is true: You became a member in 1990 or in 1992?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: I considered myself a member since the multiparty elections. About 98 per cent of the Croatian population voted for the HDZ. But I became an official member in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That explains the situation very well. You were vice-president of the local commune; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BLAZ PARADZIK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The local commune of Prud is one of the local communes that altogether create the municipality of Bosanski Samac; is that correct?
